correctness.rationale: Independently rebuilt all faces from the exact 21 named tetrahedra, giving f-vector (10,38,50,21), and verified 21 distinct facets. An exact dynamic program evaluates recursive facet deletion/shellability for all 2^21-1 nonempty tetrahedron facet subsets, including non-shellability of the full complex; every one of 2^20-1 unordered nontrivial complementary partitions is then checked for two shellable sides, intersection maximal faces all triangles and recursively shellable 2-dimensional intersection. Fresh independent implementation reported exactly 247 valid partitions, six block-size counts 3/10/23/40/74/97, three size-five blocks and four-triangle interfaces matching RESULT.md. The source checker was independently read and its recurrence verified. This is a complete finite classification, not a sample or timeout inference.
residual_risks: The self-contained census applies to this fixed combinatorial ball and specifically defined two-shellable interface, not all recursive constructibility trees.
The exact enumerator is executable standard-library Python and not a formal proof of the topological type; latter is provided by Ziegler.

value.rationale: Ziegler’s 10-vertex ball is a canonical minimal strongly nonshellable combinatorial object central to the distinction between shellability and constructibility. The finite invariant is structurally motivated: classify the smallest and all one-step assemblies into shellable pieces with shellable interface. Complete exact count, block distribution and three sharp minimum witnesses can be reused in comparisons of constructibility decompositions, without needing a general theorem.
residual_risks: Not the set of all arbitrary recursive constructibility trees; no geometric-realization classification asserted.

final_claim: For the specified 21 facets of Ziegler’s 10-vertex strongly non-shellable 3-ball, exactly 247 unordered complementary partitions split it into two shellable tetrahedral subcomplexes with shellable pure 2-dimensional intersection; block-size histogram is (5+16:3,6+15:10,7+14:23,8+13:40,9+12:74,10+11:97), and exactly the three stated size-five partitions attain the minimum.
limitations: The shellability enumeration is exhaustive for exactly this labeled facet set; all face equations use exact finite set arithmetic.
